blocks.text: Lots and land in Willoughby Heights

items.t: R-CL compact lots (Zoning Bylaw No. 2500, s.403): the Residential Compact Lot Zone is Willoughby's compact-lot pattern, covering both front-loaded lots and rear-loaded lots with rear lane access. Under s.403.7, lots run from a minimum lot area of 220 m² to a maximum lot area of 464.5 m² (5% of lots not fronting a street/cul-de-sac radius may exceed the maximum), with minimum lot frontage of 11 m for front-loaded lots and 8.2 m for rear-loaded lots, minimum corner frontage 13.5 m / 12.5 m, minimum lot depth 18 m / 22 m, and panhandle lots not permitted. Verify which pattern a lot is — front-loaded vs rear-loaded changes garage, parking and lane expectations.

Tenure of the detached streets: freehold (fee-simple) — detached streets are freehold; condos and townhomes are strata under the Strata Property Act. A fee-simple lot carries NO strata, NO Form B and NO strata fees.

Servicing: Willoughby is an urban growth area inside the Urban Containment Boundary, built out under subdivision servicing standards — all lots created by subdivision in the residential zones must comply with the Township's Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw 2019 No. 5382, as amended (stated in Zoning Bylaw ss.401.8, 403.7 and 403.9). No well/septic position is documented for Willoughby lots in the research, and none is asserted — this is serviced urban ground as the bylaws frame it; a specific lot's connections are confirmed with the Township.

ALR / flood: Willoughby is an urban growth area inside the Urban Containment Boundary; ALR land inside Willoughby is NOT confirmed in the research, and a floodplain designation for specific Willoughby parcels is not confirmed — both are parcel-level checks, and no ALR split is stated. Yorkson Creek runs through the east side, and Township materials flag hazards around greenways and creeks in the plan area — check creek/greenway setbacks on east-side lots.

The form exists in the bylaw: s.403.7 governs "all fee simple and bareland strata lots created by subdivision" in R-CL — bare-land strata subdivision is a contemplated form on Willoughby's compact lots, on the same 220–464.5 m² lot table.
Named Willoughby bare-land strata community: none verified

Willoughby Community Plan frame: the Willoughby Community Plan is Bylaw 1836 (1979), now Schedule 6 to Bylaw 6200 (adopted Dec 1, 2025). The Transit Corridor is the high-density spine of the area in the update materials. Unbuilt plan designations are not lots for sale.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Willoughby Heights

items.t: Municipality: Township of Langley, BC. The Township's official planning name for the area is "Willoughby"; "Willoughby Heights" is the name the board's data uses for this sub-area (SnapStats FVR September 2026 report). The name Willoughby was suggested for the post office at the corner of 208 Street and 83 Avenue after the settler Willoughby, per the Township schools history document held by SD35.

Boundaries, per the Willoughby Community Plan Area description in Bylaw No. 6201: bordered by the municipal boundary with the City of Surrey to the southwest, Highway 1 to the north, the ridgeline of the Trans Mountain Pipeline right-of-way and Lower Mainland Regional Park and 68 Avenue to the south, and 216 Street and the Willowbrook Connector to the east; this description supersedes the older Bylaw No. 3800 description (200 Street, 208 Street, Highway 1, 62 Avenue and Fraser Highway).

Main roads: Highway 1 along the north boundary with the 200 Street, 208 Street and 216 Street interchanges; 200 Street, 208 Street, 80 Avenue (Willoughby Way), 72 Avenue, 76 Avenue, 84 Avenue and 86 Avenue are the main streets named in the plan. Transit: route 501 (Surrey Central–Langley Centre via Fraser Highway and 200 Street), route 372 (Clayton Heights–Langley Centre via 72 Avenue), route 595 (Langley Centre–Maple Ridge via the Golden Ears Bridge); hubs at Langley Events Centre / Carvolth Exchange.

Schools — SD35 chains as documented in the research: for the sample address 7888 200 Street, the SD35 School Locator returns Donna Gabriel Robins Elementary → Peter Ewart Middle School → R.E. Mountain Secondary. Schools physically in Willoughby with SD35 addresses: Donna Gabriel Robins Elementary, 7844 204B Street; Lynn Fripps Elementary, 21020 83 Avenue; Township statements also name Willoughby Elementary, Yorkson Creek Middle School and R.E. Mountain Secondary as Willoughby schools. Catchments are address-based — other addresses may differ, and no home is promised a specific school.
Post-secondary: Trinity Western University's Smith campus is at 8086 – 208 Street, and the university's campus expansion in southeast Willoughby is named in the Township's phase-1 background paper.

Market context, labelled correctly: SnapStats FVR September 2026 — Willoughby Heights detached inventory 100 / solds 13 / ratio 13%; attached inventory 369 / solds 70 / ratio 19%. Langley (Township + City combined) community detached median $1,345,000 and attached median $611,000.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Willoughby Heights

items.t: Zoning + plan frame: Township of Langley Zoning Bylaw No. 2500 (R-CL s.403 in Sections 1–2); Willoughby Community Plan = Bylaw 1836 (1979), now Schedule 6 to Bylaw 6200 (adopted Dec 1, 2025); Plan Update Bylaws 6201/6202/6203 at first/second reading May 25, 2026 only — never upgrade reading-stage bylaws, and live-page tiles presenting June 15, 2026 repeals by 6202/6203 as done are UNVERIFIED.

SSMUH (Township): Bylaw 6020, adopted Nov 18, 2024 — NO 6-plex tier exists in it: (The bylaw's amendments are visible in the Zoning Bylaw text itself, tagged "#6020 18/11/24" through ss.401–404.) Secondary suite cap 120 m². The Township's provincial SSMUH rules apply on eligible Willoughby lots as stated in the Township-wide SSMUH material.

Coach houses — fee-simple, never strata, with a live conflict flagged: a coach house is a fee-simple second unit on a detached lot under Zoning Bylaw 2500 s.102 — never strata, never a townhouse complex. Live conflict, flagged not resolved: s.102 (July 2025) permits townhouse suites at 120 m² vs the Township's January 2025 guide saying not permitted. Willoughby's plans carry rear-lane (coach) houses as an alternate housing form on compact R-CL lots.

Strata block (the area's strata stock, and any bare-land strata lot in full): Form B diligence (fees, amounts owed, levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022 (directory "rentals not allowed" lines for Willow Park Estates and Highgate Terrace are void for long-term rentals on exactly this ground); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions. A listing's "45+" line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw. Highgate Terrace (19645 64 Avenue) is age-restricted with the exact age UNCONFIRMED — never state it as 55+.

ALR rules: no ALR ground inside Willoughby is confirmed in the research, so no ALR rule is applied to a Willoughby parcel here. Standing rules, for completeness only where ALR ground were ever confirmed on a Langley parcel: ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; residence caps principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha); farm class three-tier ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.

blocks.text: Good to know about Willoughby Heights

items.t: The bylaw's own table is the correction to two circulating figures: 464.5 m² in s.403.7 is a maximum LOT area (with a 5% cul-de-sac exception), not a building floor-area cap — and a "355 m²" cap appears nowhere in the bylaw text read. Anyone pricing a Willoughby lot off either wrong version mis-sizes the land. (Re-read Nov 2, 2026.)

Willoughby's age-restricted stock predates Willoughby: Willow Park Estates (1987) and Highgate Terrace (1990) were built decades before the Transit Corridor and Town Centre build-out, at the area's southwest edge near Willowbrook — and Highgate Terrace's age restriction has no published age, so it is UNCONFIRMED as 55+.

The plan area's boundary moved on paper: the Bylaw 6201 description (Highway 1 north; Surrey boundary southwest; pipeline ridgeline / 68 Avenue south; 216 Street / Willowbrook Connector east) supersedes the older Bylaw 3800 description — a lot near an edge can be inside one description and outside the other.

No grocery store or shopping centre name with an address was confirmed on an official source for Willoughby in the research — UNVERIFIED, despite the Town Centre's prominence in search language. The library that does check out: Muriel Arnason Library, 130 – 20338 65 Avenue (FVRL).

faq.q: Which schools serve a Willoughby address?
faq.a: For the sample address 7888 200 Street, the SD35 School Locator returns Donna Gabriel Robins Elementary, Peter Ewart Middle School and R.E. Mountain Secondary; other addresses may fall in different catchments, and Township sources also name Willoughby Elementary and Yorkson Creek Middle School as Willoughby schools.

faq.q: What did the Willoughby plan update change?
faq.a: Bylaws No. 6201, 6202 and 6203 replaced the Willoughby Community Plan and created the Willoughby Transit Corridor Plan and the Gordon Neighbourhood Plan.

faq.q: Where is the Langley Events Centre?
faq.a: At 7888 200 Street in Willoughby, a Township-owned multi-purpose sports and events facility, per the Township.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Willoughby Heights?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board figures showed 100 houses listed with 13 sold in the month and 369 condos and townhomes listed with 70 sold in the month in Willoughby Heights. Those are month-end counts and move daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Willoughby Heights a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In September 2026, houses had a sales ratio of 13%, a balanced market; condos and townhomes had a sales ratio of 19%, a balanced market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How big is a Willoughby lot, really?
faq.a: Under R-CL s.403.7: minimum lot area 220 m², maximum 464.5 m², frontage at least 11 m front-loaded or 8.2 m rear-loaded, depth at least 18 m / 22 m, no panhandles. Those are the subdivision table figures for lots created in the zone — measure the actual lot against title.

faq.q: Front-loaded or rear-loaded — why does it matter?
faq.a: It changes where the garage and parking sit, whether there is a lane, and the frontage/depth minimums that applied when the lot was created (11 m / 18 m vs 8.2 m / 22 m). Price lane access and parking accordingly.

faq.q: Is a coach house a strata unit I can buy separately?
faq.a: No. A coach house is a fee-simple second unit on the detached lot under Zoning Bylaw 2500 s.102 — it is part of the lot's ownership, never strata and never separately titled as a complex. Note the flagged live conflict on townhouse suites (s.102 July 2025 vs the Township's January 2025 guide) before relying on suite potential.

faq.q: Can I subdivide a Willoughby lot?
faq.a: Only against the zone table plus the Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw 2019 No. 5382 — and on R-CL lots of 220–464.5 m² there is no room left to split.

faq.q: How many units can I put on a detached lot?
faq.a: Township SSMUH is Bylaw 6020 (adopted Nov 18, 2024), and NO 6-plex tier exists in it; the secondary suite cap is 120 m². Check the lot's eligibility in the Township's SSMUH material.
